summary: The total force (fx/fy/fz), its accumulation onto i and j, and the torque accumulation are all computed INSIDE the `if (rsq < cut_coulsq_ij)` block, so for any pair with cut_coul <= r < cut_lj the LJ force is computed but silently discarded, while the LJ energy is still tallied.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut_kokkos.cpp:320 opens `if (rsq < cut_coulsq_ij) {` and line 434 closes it (`} // cutsq_coulsq_ij`); lines 400-421 -- `KK_FLOAT fq = factor_coul*qqrd2e; fx = fq*forcecoulx + delx*forcelj; ... fx_i += fx; ... a_f(j,0) -= fx;` -- sit inside that block, while `forcelj` is computed at lines 303-306 under the separate `if (rsq < cut_ljsq_ij)`. The CPU style src/DIPOLE/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut.cpp closes the coul block at line 203 and only THEN does `fq = factor_coul*qqrd2e; fx = fq*forcecoulx + delx*forcelj;` (lines 215-218) and the f/torque accumulation (lines 222-236). The same defect is repeated in the team kernel: block opened at line 561, closed at line 669, with fx/fy/fz assigned at lines 642-644 inside it while `fx` is initialised to 0 at line 517 and accumulated at line 674 outside.
failure_scenario: `pair_style lj/cut/dipole/cut/kk 10.0 6.0` (cut_lj 10, cut_coul 6, both legal; cutsq = max(cut_lj,cut_coul)^2 per src/DIPOLE/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut.cpp init_one): every pair with 6 <= r < 10 contributes its LJ energy to eng_vdwl but zero force and zero virial, so forces do not match the energy, energy is not conserved, and results differ from the CPU style.
suggested_fix: Move the `fq`/`fx`/`fy`/`fz` computation, the i- and j-side force and torque accumulation out of the `if (rsq < cut_coulsq_ij)` block (to just before the ev_tally_xyz call), exactly as the CPU style does, in both the range and the team kernel.

summary: evdwl and ecoul are only evaluated when eflag_global is set, so when only per-atom energy is requested (eflag_atom without eflag_global) ev_tally_xyz receives epair = 0 and all per-atom pair energies come out zero.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut_kokkos.cpp:307 `if (eflag_global) { evdwl = ...; ev.evdwl += ...; }` and line 423 `if (EVFLAG && eflag_global) { ecoul = ...; ev.ecoul += ...; }`, while line 436-437 `if (EVFLAG && (eflag_atom || vflag_either)) ev_tally_xyz<...>(ev, i, j, ecoul+evdwl, ...)` uses those variables (initialised to 0 at lines 285-286). The CPU style src/DIPOLE/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut.cpp:238 guards the same computation with `if (eflag)` (i.e. eflag_either), and src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:180 and 264 likewise use `c.eflag_either`. Repeated at lines 548 and 658 in the team kernel.
failure_scenario: `compute pe/atom` dumped on a timestep on which no global energy is needed (Verlet::ev_set gives eflag = ENERGY_ATOM only, eflag_global = 0): every atom's pair energy is reported as 0.0 instead of its real value.
suggested_fix: Change both guards to `eflag_either` (keeping the ev.evdwl / ev.ecoul reduction updates themselves under eflag_global).

summary: In the team kernel the per-atom force/torque update after the ThreadVectorRange reduction is not wrapped in Kokkos::single(Kokkos::PerThread(team),...), so every vector lane executes the read-modify-write on f(i,*) and torque(i,*).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut_kokkos.cpp:501 `Kokkos::parallel_reduce(Kokkos::ThreadVectorRange(team, jnum), [&](...){...}, fx_i, fy_i, fz_i, torquex_i, torquey_i, torquez_i);` is followed at lines 684-689 by bare `a_f(i,0) += fx_i; ... a_torque(i,2) += torquez_i;`. The canonical pattern in src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:354-358 wraps exactly this update: `Kokkos::single(Kokkos::PerThread(team), [&] () { a_f(i,0) += fsum.x; ... });` (and pair_kokkos.h:309-314 for the ZEROFLAG store).
failure_scenario: GPU run with `-k on ... -pk kokkos neigh full` plus the autotuner enabled and newton off (the only path that selects the team policy, lines 188-200): with vectorsize > 1 and independent thread scheduling the non-atomic `f(i,0) += fx_i` from the lanes of a warp can interleave, giving forces that are a multiple of the correct value on some atoms.
suggested_fix: Wrap the six post-reduction accumulations in `Kokkos::single(Kokkos::PerThread(team), [&] () { ... });` as pair_kokkos.h does.

summary: The total force (fq/fx/fy/fz) and the whole force+torque accumulation sit INSIDE the 'if (rsq < cut_coulsq_ij)' block, which closes only at :434. For any pair with cut_coul <= r < cut_lj the LJ force is computed and then silently discarded, while the LJ energy is still tallied and ev_tally_xyz is called with fx=fy=fz=0 (so the virial is lost too). Repeated in the team kernel (block :561-:669, accumulation at :642-644).
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut_kokkos.cpp:303-306 computes forcelj in its own cut_ljsq block, :400-421 do the total force and accumulation inside the coul block, :436-437 call ev_tally_xyz outside it. The CPU style src/DIPOLE/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut.cpp:206-210 closes the LJ block with 'else forcelj = 0.0;' and only then, at :215-236, computes fq/fx/fy/fz and accumulates - unconditionally.)

summary: evdwl and ecoul are computed only under eflag_global, but ev_tally_xyz is called under (eflag_atom || vflag_either), so on a per-atom-energy-only timestep every per-atom pair energy is tallied as zero. Same family as the confirmed pair_dpd_kokkos.cpp:370 defect.
verified_by: orchestrator (guards at src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut_kokkos.cpp:307 and :423 vs the call at :436-437; the CPU style guards with eflag (=eflag_either) at src/DIPOLE/pair_lj_cut_dipole_cut.cpp:238).

summary: With bzeroflag=1, chemflag=1 and wselfallflag=0 the KOKKOS evaluate_bi() subtracts bzero[j] from EVERY diagonal element triple (elem1==elem2==elem3), whereas the CPU SNA::compute_bi() subtracts it only from the one triple built from the central atom's element ielem, so pair snap/kk reports different energies than pair snap.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:1115-1125: 'register_loop<yi_batch>([&] (int n) -> void { bval[n] *= static_cast<accum_type>(2.0); if (bzero_flag) { if (!wselfall_flag) { if (elem1 == elem2 && elem1 == elem3) { bval[n] -= static_cast<accum_type>(bzero[j]); } } else { bval[n] -= static_cast<accum_type>(bzero[j]); } } });' -- evaluate_bi() never receives the central atom's element (its signature at sna_kokkos.h:340 and the caller compute_bi(iatom,jjb) at sna_kokkos_impl.h:1009 carry no ielem). src/ML-SNAP/sna.cpp:696-702: 'if (bzero_flag) { if (!wselfall_flag) { itriple = (ielem*nelements+ielem)*nelements+ielem; for (int jjb = 0; jjb < idxb_max; jjb++) { const int j = idxb[jjb].j; blist[itriple*idxb_max+jjb] -= bzero[j]; } } else { ... every triple ... } }' with ielem = the central atom's element (src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:346 'snaptr->compute_bi(ielem);'). For nelements > 1 the KOKKOS code shifts nelements diagonal triples instead of one. No compensating correction exists elsewhere: 'grep -n bzero src/KOKKOS/*' only matches sna_kokkos{.h,_impl.h}. blist feeds the energy directly (pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:1418 'evdwl += static_cast<accum_type>(d_coeffi[icoeff+1]*snaKK.blist(ii,idx_chem,idxb));').
failure_scenario: A multi-element SNAP potential with 'chemflag 1 bzeroflag 1 wselfallflag 0' (all legal; only wselfallflag differs from the shipped potentials/InP_JCPA2020.snapparam, which uses wselfallflag 1 and therefore hides the bug): every atom's energy is off by the constant -sum_{e != ielem} sum_jjb coeff_ielem[(e,e,e)*idxb_max+jjb+1]*bzero[j], so pair snap/kk and pair snap report different potential energies for the same configuration. Because the offset is position-independent, forces and stresses are unaffected, which is why force-based regression tests do not catch it.
suggested_fix: Pass the central atom's element into compute_bi()/evaluate_bi() (it is already available to the caller as d_map(type(i))) and gate the !wselfall_flag subtraction on 'elem1 == elem2 && elem2 == elem3 && elem1 == ielem', matching sna.cpp:698.

summary: SNAKokkos::compute_dsfac(), a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION, calls unqualified sin()/cos() instead of Kokkos::sin/Kokkos::cos, violating the KOKKOS device-math rule and silently promoting single-precision arguments to double; the function is also dead code.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:2265 'dsfac_outer = -onehalf * sin((r - rmin0) * rcutfac) * rcutfac;', :2283 'sfac_outer = onehalf * (cos((r - rmin0) * rcutfac) + one);', :2290 'sfac_inner = onehalf * (one - cos(static_cast<real_type>(MY_PI2) + (r - sinner) * rcutfac));', :2291 'dsfac_inner = onehalf * rcutfac * sin(...);'. The sibling routines do it correctly: compute_sfac uses 'Kokkos::cos' (:2231) and compute_s_dsfac uses 'Kokkos::sin'/'Kokkos::cos' (:2316-2317, :2328-2329). .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels ... never std::'. Grepping the package shows compute_dsfac is never called (only compute_sfac at :846 and compute_s_dsfac at :374 and :1832 are used).
failure_scenario: No current runtime effect because the function is unreachable; if it is ever wired back in, a SYCL/HIP build may fail to resolve the unqualified name and a real_type=float build loses precision through double promotion.
suggested_fix: Either delete compute_dsfac (and its declaration at sna_kokkos.h:372) since compute_s_dsfac supersedes it, or qualify the four calls with Kokkos::.

summary: memory_usage() selects the GPU vs CPU array set with 'if constexpr (!host_flag)' while grow_rij() allocates them under '!host_flag && !legacy_on_gpu', so with legacy_on_gpu enabled the reported memory omits the two largest arrays and counts five 1x1x1 dummies instead.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:323-339 'if (!host_flag && !legacy_on_gpu) { ...realloc a_gpu/b_gpu/da_gpu/db_gpu/sfac_gpu at full size...; realloc ulist_cpu/dulist_cpu at 1,1,1; } else { ...a_gpu etc at 1,1(,1)...; realloc ulist_cpu/dulist_cpu at natom_pad, nmax, idxu_cache_max; }' versus :2360-2369 'if constexpr (!host_flag) { bytes += MemKK::memory_usage(a_gpu); ... } else { bytes += MemKK::memory_usage(ulist_cpu); bytes += MemKK::memory_usage(dulist_cpu); }'. legacy_on_gpu is a runtime member (sna_kokkos.h:474) initialised from the owner (pair_snap_kokkos.h:87 'static constexpr bool legacy_on_gpu = false;'), so the two conditions only agree while that knob stays false.
failure_scenario: Flip pair_snap_kokkos.h's legacy_on_gpu to true (its documented purpose: 'run the CPU path on the GPU') and 'info memory'/the pair style's memory_usage() under-reports by natom_pad*nmax*idxu_cache_max*sizeof(complex)*4, the dominant allocation. No wrong physics.
suggested_fix: Use the same predicate in memory_usage(): 'if constexpr (!host_flag) if (!legacy_on_gpu) {gpu arrays} else {cpu arrays}', or factor the predicate into a single helper used by both.

summary: sna_kokkos_impl.h redefines MY_PI and MY_PI2 as file-static doubles directly in namespace LAMMPS_NS instead of using MathConst, giving every translation unit its own copy and setting up an ambiguity with MathConst::MY_PI.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:29-30 'static const double MY_PI  = 3.14159265358979323846; // pi' and 'static const double MY_PI2  = 1.57079632679489661923; // pi/2', inside 'namespace LAMMPS_NS {' (line 27). src/math_const.h already provides LAMMPS_NS::MathConst::MY_PI and MY_PI2 with the same values; the CPU counterpart src/ML-SNAP/sna.cpp:23,31 does '#include "math_const.h"' + 'using namespace MathConst;'. Because this header is pulled into pair_snap_kokkos.cpp, compute_sna_grid_kokkos.cpp and compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos.cpp, any of those adding 'using namespace MathConst;' would make an unqualified MY_PI ambiguous.
failure_scenario: No current runtime effect. A later edit that adds 'using namespace MathConst;' to any TU including sna_kokkos.h fails to compile with an ambiguous-name error that points at an unrelated line.
suggested_fix: Delete the two definitions and use MathConst::MY_PI / MathConst::MY_PI2 (already available via math_const.h).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 08
summary: With bzeroflag=1, chemflag=1, wselfallflag=0, evaluate_bi() subtracts bzero[j] from every diagonal element triple (elem1==elem2==elem3) instead of only the central atom's element triple as SNA::compute_bi() does, shifting every atom's SNAP energy by a constant for multi-element potentials.
evidence: sna_kokkos_impl.h:1115-1126 (no ielem available); src/ML-SNAP/sna.cpp:696-702 uses itriple built from ielem.
failure_scenario: Multi-element SNAP with bzeroflag 1 and wselfallflag 0: pair snap/kk energies differ from pair snap by a position-independent offset; forces unaffected, so force-based tests do not catch it.
suggested_fix: Pass the central element into compute_bi/evaluate_bi and gate on elem1==elem2==elem3==ielem.

summary: The KOKKOS EAM styles ignore the per-type-pair scale[][] factor that the CPU PairEAM applies to force, pair energy and embedding energy, so `fix adapt ... pair eam* scale ...` silently has no effect under -sf kk.
evidence: There is no reference to `scale` anywhere in src/KOKKOS/pair_eam_kokkos.cpp or .h (grep -n scale finds only the copyright banner). CPU base src/MANYBODY/pair_eam.cpp applies it in three places: line 295 `fpair = -scale[itype][jtype]*psip*recip;` vs KOKKOS pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:815 `const KK_FLOAT fpair = -psip*recip;`; line 306 `if (eflag) evdwl = scale[itype][jtype]*phi;` vs pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:829/1059 which tally bare `phi`; and line 361 `phi *= scale[type[i]][type[i]];` in compute_embedding() vs pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:649-650/725-726/934-935 which tally the unscaled embedding phi. PairEAM::extract() (pair_eam.cpp:1679) still hands the scale array to fix adapt, and fix_adapt.cpp:428-432 resolves the /kk-suffixed style, so the fix writes values nobody reads. doc/src/fix_adapt.rst:191 documents `pair eam, eam/alloy, eam/fs ... scale ... type pairs`. The /omp (OPENMP/pair_eam_omp.cpp:236,310,321) and /opt (OPT/pair_eam_opt.cpp:284,366,377) variants do apply it.
failure_scenario: `pair_style eam/alloy/kk` + `fix adapt 1 pair eam/alloy scale 1 1 v_lambda` (thermodynamic integration): forces and energies are computed with scale==1 for the whole run, so the free-energy integration result is wrong, with no error or warning.
suggested_fix: Add a device-resident scale table (e.g. a DualView filled in an init_one() override, like the other /kk styles do for their params) and multiply fpair, the pair phi and the embedding phi by it, matching pair_eam.cpp:295, 306 and 361.

summary: PairEAMKokkos::array2spline() overrides the base without ever allocating the host frho_spline/rhor_spline/z2r_spline arrays, yet the style inherits atomic_energy_enable=1, so PairEAM::compute_atomic_energy() dereferences null pointers when fix sgcmc uses it.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:384-418 `void PairEAMKokkos<DeviceType>::array2spline() { rdr = 1.0/dr; rdrho = 1.0/drho; ... }` builds only the Kokkos DualViews and never calls PairEAM::array2spline(), which is the only place the host arrays are created (src/MANYBODY/pair_eam.cpp: `memory->create(frho_spline,nfrho,nrho+1,7,"pair:frho"); memory->create(rhor_spline,...); memory->create(z2r_spline,...)`); they stay at the nullptr set in PairEAM's constructor (pair_eam.cpp:67-69). The KOKKOS constructor (pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:44-51) clears respa_enable and single_enable but leaves atomic_energy_enable at the 1 set by PairEAM::PairEAM (pair_eam.cpp:42). PairEAM::compute_atomic_energy (pair_eam.cpp:410,415,424) does `coeff = z2r_spline[type2z2r[jtype][itype]][m];`, `coeff = rhor_spline[...][m];` and `coeff = frho_spline[type2frho[itype]][m];`. src/MC/fix_sgcmc.cpp:259 only checks `if (!force->pair->atomic_energy_enable) error->all(...)` and then calls it at lines 1040-1062.
failure_scenario: `pair_style eam/alloy/kk` (or eam/kk, eam/fs/kk, eam/he/kk) together with `fix sgcmc ... ` in atomic-energy mode: the guard passes and the first swap attempt dereferences a null z2r_spline -> segmentation fault. The same nullptr also makes PairEAM::single() unusable, though single_enable=0 hides that.
suggested_fix: Set `atomic_energy_enable = 0;` in the PairEAMKokkos constructor, or have array2spline() call PairEAM::array2spline() first so the host spline tables exist.

summary: The HIP TeamPolicy variant of EAM kernel C calls the unqualified `sqrt` in device code instead of `Kokkos::sqrt`, unlike every other square root in the file.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_eam_kokkos.cpp:1005 `const KK_FLOAT r = sqrt(rsq);` inside `operator()(TagPairEAMKernelC<...>, const typename Kokkos::TeamPolicy<DeviceType>::member_type&, EV_FLOAT&)`. The equivalent RangePolicy kernel uses `Kokkos::sqrt` (line 776 `const KK_FLOAT r = Kokkos::sqrt(rsq);`), as do lines 602, 696 and 901. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: "Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels ... never std::".
failure_scenario: Under LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE the unqualified overload can bind to the double version and silently widen/narrow; on toolchains where <cmath>'s sqrt is not visible as a device function the HIP build fails to compile.
suggested_fix: Change line 1005 to `const KK_FLOAT r = Kokkos::sqrt(rsq);`.

summary: The KOKKOS EAM styles drop the CPU style's 'per-atom density exceeded rhomax' warning, so a user gets no notice that the embedding table was linearly extrapolated.
evidence: CPU src/MANYBODY/pair_eam.cpp:316-324 tracks beyond_rhomax in compute_embedding() (line 359 `if (!HE) beyond_rhomax = 1;`) and does `MPI_Allreduce(&beyond_rhomax,&exceeded_rhomax,1,MPI_INT,MPI_SUM,world); if (exceeded_rhomax) ... error->warning(FLERR,"A per-atom density exceeded rhomax of EAM potential table - a linear extrapolation to the energy was made");`. src/KOKKOS/pair_eam_kokkos.cpp performs the same extrapolation at lines 647-648, 723-724 and 932-933 (`else if (d_rho[i] > rhomax_kk) phi += d_fp[i] * (d_rho[i]-rhomax_kk);`) but never sets or reduces any flag, and compute() (lines 201-318) has no corresponding warning.
failure_scenario: An EAM run under -sf kk in which atoms come close enough to exceed rhomax produces extrapolated energies identical to the CPU run but without the diagnostic warning, so the user does not learn the table was exceeded.
suggested_fix: Reduce a beyond_rhomax flag out of kernel B/AB (e.g. an extra int in the reduction or a small device flag view) and issue the same MPI_Allreduce + warning as pair_eam.cpp:316-324.

summary: The KOKKOS EAM styles never reference the per-type-pair scale[][] factor. The CPU PairEAM applies it to fpair, evdwl and the embedding energy, so 'fix adapt ... pair eam* scale ...' silently has no effect under -sf kk.
verified_by: orchestrator (grep 'scale' over src/KOKKOS/pair_eam_kokkos.{cpp,h} returns only the license header; src/MANYBODY/pair_eam.cpp:295, :306, :361 apply it). Same family as the confirmed meam/kk d_scale defect.

summary: The DSF self-energy is computed on the host from `atom->q[i]`, but compute() only syncs q to the DEVICE (`atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read)`); on a GPU build the host q array is stale after every device-side exchange/sort, so eng_coul and eatom get self-energies from the wrong charges.
failure_scenario: GPU run `-k on g 1 -sf kk` with `pair_style born/coul/dsf/kk` on >1 MPI rank: after the first reneighbor, atoms have migrated and the host atom->q[0..nlocal) still holds the previous step's charges (and the previous nlocal), so the sum of q_i^2 -- and therefore the reported Coulomb energy -- is wrong; the per-atom energies are wrong even on 1 rank as soon as atom sorting permutes d_q.
suggested_fix: Move the self-energy into the device kernel using the `q` device view (as pair_coul_dsf_kokkos does), or at minimum call `atomKK->sync(Host,Q_MASK)` before the host loops and iterate over the neighbor list's ilist rather than 0..nlocal.

summary: The DSF self-energy is accumulated on the host from atom->q[i] (also at :150 for eatom) although compute() syncs only the device copy. On a GPU build with device-resident sorting/exchange the host q array is stale, so eng_coul and the per-atom energy use the wrong charges.
verified_by: orchestrator (:88 syncs execution_space only; :121 and :150 read atom->q[i]). The intended KOKKOS idiom computes the self-energy inside the kernel from the device q view - see pair_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:231-235. Same defect in pair_born_coul_dsf_cs_kokkos.cpp:126, pair_born_coul_wolf_kokkos.cpp:121 and pair_born_coul_wolf_cs_kokkos.cpp:126.

summary: In the host/device force-overlap path the forces a non-KOKKOS (legacy Host) force style writes into atom->f are never transferred into the Kokkos host buffer before the merge, so on builds where k_f needs a transform view they are silently dropped.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.cpp:421-424 sets 'datamask_exclude = (F_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK)' whenever overlap_possible(), and 438/441 (and 467/470, 502/505) then use only the masked forms '~(~datamask_read|datamask_exclude)', so F_MASK is never passed to atomKK->modified() after the style ran.  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_atomic_kokkos.cpp:210-213 shows modified(Host, mask) only calls 'k_f.modify_host()' when the mask contains F_MASK, so TransformView::modified_legacy_hostkk stays 0.  The merge at verlet_kokkos.cpp:513-514 is 'atomKK->k_f.sync_legacy_to_hostkk(); Kokkos::deep_copy(LMPHostType(),f_merge_copy,atomKK->k_f.view_hostkk());' and src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:955-968 makes sync_legacy_to_hostkk() a no-op unless modified_legacy_hostkk is set.  A non-KOKKOS style has execution_space == Host (src/pair.cpp:128, src/kspace.cpp:98, src/bond.cpp:62) and writes atom->f, which memory_kokkos.h:119 aliases to k_f.view_host() (the legacy view), a different allocation from view_hostkk() whenever TransformView::NEED_TRANSFORM is true (kokkos_type.h:700) -- i.e. single-precision builds (KK_ACC_FLOAT=float, kokkos_type.h:401-402) or LMP_KOKKOS_LAYOUT_DEFAULT builds.  host_force_styles() (verlet_kokkos.cpp:699) deliberately accepts Host as well as HostKK, so the path is taken for such styles.  Contrast the sibling DynamicalMatrixKokkos::update_force (src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:287), which merges from k_f.view_host() (the legacy view) instead.
failure_scenario: GPU backend, single-precision KOKKOS build (or LMP_KOKKOS_LAYOUT_DEFAULT), '-sf kk' with any force style that has no /kk variant (e.g. a non-KOKKOS kspace such as pppm/cg, or an unported pair/bond style): that style's entire force contribution is added to a buffer nobody reads, the merge adds zeros, and the trajectory is silently wrong. In the non-overlap (CPU-only) path datamask_exclude is 0 and F_MASK is claimed normally, which is why CI does not see it.
suggested_fix: Claim the legacy write before the merge (e.g. call atomKK->k_f.modify_legacy_hostkk() in the execute_on_host block when any host force style has execution_space == Host), or merge from k_f.view_host() as DynamicalMatrixKokkos does; note that when both a Host and a HostKK style contributed the two buffers must be added, not deep-copied over each other.

summary: Commented-out debug sync/modified blocks ('// added debug', '// debug') remain in VerletKokkos::run() at lines 350-352, 359-361, 371-373 and 379-381.
evidence: verlet_kokkos.cpp:350-352 '// added debug / //atomKK->sync(Host,ALL_MASK); / //atomKK->modified(Host,ALL_MASK);' and three more identical blocks. Project review rules: commented-out code added for debugging purposes should be removed entirely.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; release-hygiene item flagged by the project's own review checklist.
suggested_fix: Delete the four commented-out debug blocks.

summary: The spline branch of uf_lookup_kk() reads the pad element d_e(tb,tablength)/d_f(tb,tablength)/d_e2/d_f2 which setup_tables() never fills, and the comment's claim that its weight is exactly zero is false for bond lengths in (hi, hi+delta).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_table_kokkos.cpp:77-86 allocates the 2-D views with 'tablength+1' columns 'so that the spline branch can read itable+1 at the last bin, where its weight is exactly zero', but :95-103 only fills 'for (int i = 0; i < tablength; i++)', leaving column tablength at 0. :249-265: 'const int itable = static_cast<int>((x_in - lo) * invdelta); if (itable >= tablength) { d_error_flag() = 2; return; } ... b = (x_in - d_r(tb,itable)) * invdelta; ... u = a*d_e(tb,itable) + b*d_e(tb,itable+1) + ...'. With r[i] = lo + i*delta and hi = lo + (tablength-1)*delta, itable == tablength-1 corresponds to x in [hi, hi+delta), so b = (x-hi)/delta is in [0,1) and is only zero when x == hi exactly. The CPU src/MOLECULE/bond_table.cpp:611-614 reads tb->e[itable+1] from an array of length tablength (an out-of-bounds read), so the two implementations disagree for hi < r < hi+delta.
failure_scenario: 'bond_style table spline N' with a bond stretched just past the table's outer cutoff (hi < r < hi+delta, still accepted by the itable < tablength test): bond/kk returns u and mdu computed with a zero end point, giving a different (and unphysical) energy/force than the plain bond table style.
suggested_fix: Fill the pad column with the extrapolated end values (or clamp b to 0 at itable == tablength-1) and fix the misleading comment; better yet make itable == tablength-1 raise error flag 2 like the inner cutoff, matching the intent of the table bounds.

summary: uf_lookup_kk() omits the CPU's non-finite bond-length guard, so a NaN/Inf separation produces an undefined int conversion instead of a clean error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_table_kokkos.cpp:241-252 starts straight at 'const int tb = d_tabindex[type]; ... const int itable = static_cast<int>((x_in - lo) * invdelta); if (itable < 0) { d_error_flag() = 1; return; }'. CPU src/MOLECULE/bond_table.cpp:592 begins with 'if (!std::isfinite(x)) { error->one(FLERR, "Illegal bond in bond style table"); }'.
failure_scenario: A blown-up trajectory gives r = NaN: static_cast<int>(NaN) is undefined; on x86 it yields INT_MIN so the code happens to report 'Bond length < table inner cutoff', but on other targets it can produce an in-range itable and silently index the table with garbage instead of aborting.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (!Kokkos::isfinite(x_in)) { d_error_flag() = 1; return; }' (or a third flag value with its own message) at the top of uf_lookup_kk().

summary: PairBondValVecKokkos::settings() replaces the base argument check with `narg > 3` and hard-codes `PairBondValVec::settings(2,arg)`, so too-few arguments are never rejected and arg[1] is read out of bounds, while a bogus 3rd argument is silently ignored.
failure_scenario: `pair_style bondval/vec/kk 6.0` (narg==1) makes the base read arg[1], a stale pointer left over in Input::arg -> garbage cut_global or a segfault; `pair_style bondval/vec/kk 6.0 4.0 extra` is accepted with `extra` silently ignored while the CPU style errors.
suggested_fix: Forward narg unchanged (`PairBondValVec::settings(narg,arg);`) or validate `narg != 2` with utils::missing_cmd_args().

summary: Two commented-out debugging printf() calls left in the device kernel.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_bondval_vec_kokkos.cpp:601: `  //printf("i: %d, d_Di(i,0): %f, d_Di(i,1): %f, d_Di(i,2): %f\n", i, d_Di(i,0), d_Di(i,1), d_Di(i,2));` and :605: `    //printf("i: %d, phi: %f", i, phi);`.  The project review rules state that commented-out code added for debugging must be removed entirely, and that printf() must not appear in new code.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; a code-review/style rule violation that would be flagged on the PR.
suggested_fix: Delete both commented-out printf lines.

summary: MathSpecialKokkos::factorial() is declared extern in the header but is defined nowhere and called nowhere, so any use would be a link error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/math_special_kokkos.h:34 'extern double factorial(const int n);' with the doc comment promising a table lookup for 0 <= n <= 167. src/KOKKOS/math_special_kokkos.cpp defines only 'double MathSpecialKokkos::erfcx_y100(const double y100)' (line 61) -- the nfac_table[] and the factorial() definition that src/math_special.cpp:10-199 carries were not ported. 'grep -rn "MathSpecialKokkos::factorial" src/' finds nothing; the KOKKOS styles that need factorials use their own copies (src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:1910, and compute_orientorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:38 which pulls in the non-KOKKOS MathSpecial::factorial).
failure_scenario: A future KOKKOS style that calls MathSpecialKokkos::factorial() compiles cleanly and then fails at link time with an undefined reference.
suggested_fix: Remove the declaration, or port the nfac_table[] lookup from src/math_special.cpp into math_special_kokkos.cpp.

summary: The header defines the object-like macro FM_DOUBLE_LOG2OFE and never undefines it, leaking it into every translation unit that includes math_special_kokkos.h.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/math_special_kokkos.h:59 '#define FM_DOUBLE_LOG2OFE  1.4426950408889634074'. The non-KOKKOS original keeps the same constant out of the header and as a typed constant in the implementation file: src/math_special.cpp has 'static constexpr double FM_DOUBLE_LOG2OFE = 1.4426950408889634074;'.
failure_scenario: Any translation unit that includes both math_special_kokkos.h and a file declaring an identifier named FM_DOUBLE_LOG2OFE (e.g. src/math_special.cpp's static constexpr, were it ever pulled in) fails to compile with a confusing macro-expansion error.
suggested_fix: Replace the macro with 'static constexpr double FM_DOUBLE_LOG2OFE = 1.4426950408889634074;' inside the MathSpecialKokkos namespace.

summary: PairPOD::~PairPOD() lacks the mandatory 'if (copymode) return;' guard required of every base class a KOKKOS style inherits from.
evidence: src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:107-159 starts directly with 'memory->destroy(rij);' - no copymode check - while PairPODKokkos sets copymode = 1 during compute (src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:208) and its own destructor does have the guard (pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:76).  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 1 requires the guard in the base-class destructor.
failure_scenario: Any future functor that captures the pair object by value (the standard KOKKOS pattern) would run ~PairPOD on the copy and free the original's memory -> double free / GPU crash.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (copymode) return;' as the first line of PairPOD::~PairPOD().

summary: PairPOD::~PairPOD() has no `if (copymode) return;` guard although PairPODKokkos derives from it and sets copymode = 1 around its kernels.
evidence: src/ML-POD/pair_pod.cpp:107-157: `PairPOD::~PairPOD() { memory->destroy(rij); ... memory->destroy(elemindex); delete fastpodptr; if (allocated) { memory->destroy(setflag); memory->destroy(cutsq); } }` -- no guard. src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.h:33 `class PairPODKokkos : public PairPOD`; src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:74-80 `~PairPODKokkos() { if (copymode) return; ... }` and :208 `copymode = 1;` show the style is meant to be copy-safe. src/KOKKOS/pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:131-137 `PairPODKokkos::coeff()` calls `PairPOD::coeff(narg,arg)`, which allocates fastpodptr and (via PairPOD::allocate, called from pair_pod_kokkos.cpp:163) setflag/cutsq, so the base really does own memory. Contrast the guarded base destructors src/pair.cpp:138, src/fix.cpp:120, src/ML-SNAP/... .
failure_scenario: Not reachable today: pair_pod_kokkos.cpp uses only KOKKOS_LAMBDA with local shadow views and never passes *this to a kernel nor uses pair_compute<>/PairComputeFunctor, so no copy of the style is ever destroyed. It becomes a double free (fastpodptr deleted twice, setflag/cutsq freed twice) the moment anyone converts a kernel to the usual `*this` functor form, which the existing `copymode = 1` at line 208 already advertises as safe.
suggested_fix: Add `if (copymode) return;` as the first statement of PairPOD::~PairPOD().

summary: ThirdOrderKokkos::update_force() treats only styles with execution_space == Host as host styles, whereas VerletKokkos::host_force_styles() also treats HostKK (the kk/host variants); a kk/host pair style combined with a device bonded style therefore never gets its forces merged into the device force array.
evidence: third_order_kokkos.cpp:172-207 test 'force->pair->execution_space==Host' (and the same for bond/angle/dihedral/improper/kspace); verlet_kokkos.cpp:697-702 uses '(style->execution_space != HostKK) && (style->execution_space != Host)' to decide. With a HostKK pair style: modified(HostKK,F_MASK) at line 222, then a device bond style does modified(Device,F_MASK) at 243; the DualView's later sync(Host,F_MASK) at 308 copies device -> host and discards the pair forces (no merge, since execute_on_host is false). dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp has the same structure (not in this group).
failure_scenario: GPU build, 'pair_style lj/cut/kk/host' + 'bond_style harmonic/kk' + 'third_order ...': the third-order force constants miss the pair contribution. Unusual combination; the plain Host and plain Device cases are handled.
suggested_fix: Use the same HostKK-or-Host predicate (or reuse VerletKokkos::host_force_styles logic) in ThirdOrderKokkos and DynamicalMatrixKokkos.

summary: None of the 13 KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION declarations in this header carry the required `// NOLINTNEXTLINE` comment.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/pair_bondval_kokkos.h:67-108 and 118-121 declare e.g.
  KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION
  void operator()(TagPairBondValPackForwardComm, const int&) const;
with no preceding `// NOLINTNEXTLINE`.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md 'Common mistakes' lists 'Missing `// NOLINTNEXTLINE` before a `KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION` (required to suppress linter warnings in LAMMPS)'.  Every other pair style header in the group (e.g. pair_adp_kokkos.h:68-69, pair_beck_kokkos.h:48-49) has it; only pair_bondval_kokkos.h and pair_bondval_vec_kokkos.h are missing it among the pair styles.
failure_scenario: clang-tidy/lint runs emit warnings for these declarations.
suggested_fix: Add `// NOLINTNEXTLINE` immediately before each `KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION` line.

summary: The KOKKOS fix wall/* styles list V_MASK in datamask_read although none of them reads or writes velocities.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_lj93_kokkos.cpp declares `datamask_read = X_MASK | F_MASK | MASK_MASK | V_MASK;` while FixWallLJ93Kokkos::wall_particle (lines 145-178) binds only `d_x = atomKK->k_x...` (151), `d_f = atomKK->k_f...` (152) and `d_mask = atomKK->k_mask...` (153) and the kernel touches nothing else.  The identical unused V_MASK appears in src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_lj126_kokkos.cpp (kernel at 138-171), fix_wall_lj1043_kokkos.cpp (159-192), fix_wall_morse_kokkos.cpp (140-173), fix_wall_harmonic_kokkos.cpp (95-128), fix_wall_harmonic_outside_kokkos.cpp (89-122) and fix_wall_region_kokkos.cpp:47.
failure_scenario: No incorrect results: VerletKokkos/ModifyKokkos simply copies the whole velocity array to the execution space before every post_force of these fixes, which is pure overhead on a GPU (and it masks genuine mask errors such as the missing RADIUS_MASK in fix_wall_region_kokkos reported separately).
suggested_fix: Remove V_MASK from datamask_read in these seven wall fixes.
